title: Derby day: APR and Rayon meet with top spot on the line
excerpt: Kigali's two giants renew their rivalry at Amahoro this afternoon with only goal difference separating them at the summit.
author: Eric Nsengimana
body: Kigali's biggest fixture returns this afternoon as APR FC host Rayon Sports at Amahoro Stadium with the Rwanda Premier League summit on the line. Both sides have 42 points after 18 matches, and only APR's superior goal difference keeps the champions top.

Vincent Mashami has named an unchanged side from the win over AS Kigali, keeping faith with Gilbert Mugisha through the middle and Patrick Sibomana in behind. Rayon boss Adil Erradi has recalled Innocent Nshuti after a minor hamstring scare, with the league's top scorer starting alongside Jules Ulimwengu.

The atmosphere around Amahoro has been building since early morning. Rayon's blue-and-white supporters began gathering at the Kigali Pelé end before noon, while the APR ultras were in place hours before kick-off.

Historically this is a fixture that ignores form. Four of the last six derbies have been decided by a single goal, and two of those have come from set pieces. With so much at stake, another tight afternoon is expected.

title: Spittler names 24-man Amavubi squad for Benin qualifier
excerpt: Torsten Spittler has handed recalls to Meddie Kagere and Arthur Gitego as Rwanda prepare for a crucial AFCON qualifier.
author: Alice Mukamana
body: Rwanda head coach Torsten Spittler has named a 24-man squad for the upcoming AFCON qualifier against Benin at Amahoro Stadium.

The German coach has recalled experienced striker Meddie Kagere and in-form forward Arthur Gitego, while Djihad Bizimana retains the captain's armband. Fiacre Ntwari is the first-choice goalkeeper despite competition from Emile Ndayishimiye.

Amavubi have won their last two home qualifiers and know a win over Benin would put them in a strong position in Group D. Spittler said the squad had spent the week working on transitions and set pieces.
"We respect Benin, but we play at home in front of our supporters and our ambition is clear," Spittler said at a press conference in Kigali. The squad reports to camp on Monday.

title: Kiyovu and the quiet revolution of Jimmy Mulisa
excerpt: No signings, no noise — just one of the most organised sides in Rwanda. How Kiyovu became the league's toughest puzzle.
author: Diane Uwase
body: At the start of the season, few would have placed Kiyovu in the title conversation. Yet with more than half of the campaign gone, Jimmy Mulisa's side are third and have conceded only 17 goals — the best defensive record in the division.

The secret is structure. Kiyovu defend in a compact mid-block, deny central access and force opponents wide. In possession, Blaise Nishimwe pulls the strings while Emmanuel Mugisha occupies both centre-backs.
Mulisa has also leaned on academy graduates, giving meaningful minutes to Olivier Hakizimana and Alex Mugabo. It is a patient approach that the club's board has backed, even when results were uneven.
"We are not in a hurry," Mulisa said after the draw at Police. "This team is learning to win in different ways. The table is a consequence, not the obsession."

title: Peace Cup final confirmed for Amahoro Stadium
excerpt: Rwandan football's showpiece will be staged at the newly renovated national stadium, with APR and Mukura set to meet.
author: Eric Nsengimana
body: The Rwanda Peace Cup final will be played at Amahoro Stadium, the Rwanda Football Federation (FERWAFA) confirmed on Wednesday.
APR FC reached the final with a 3-1 win over AS Kigali, while Mukura Victory Sports upset Rayon Sports 1-0 in the other semi-final. The final is scheduled for next weekend with a 18:00 kick-off.
FERWAFA said ticketing details would be announced later this week and that a limited number of VIP seats would be made available online.
The Peace Cup winner earns a place in the following season's CAF Confederation Cup, adding significant weight to the occasion.

title: Innocent Nshuti named Player of the Month
excerpt: The Rayon Sports striker takes the award after scoring five goals in four matches, including a derby double.
author: Kevin Habimana
body: Rayon Sports forward Innocent Nshuti has been voted Rwanda Premier League Player of the Month after a prolific run in front of goal.
Nshuti scored five goals in four league games, including two in the Kigali derby. He also provided an assist in the win over Mukura and has become a key part of Torsten Spittler's Amavubi plans.
"It is a team award," Nshuti said. "My job is easy when Kevin and Jules are finding me in the box."
The 27-year-old now leads the league's scoring charts with 12 goals, three clear of APR's Gilbert Mugisha.

title: Inside the Nyamata academy producing Rwanda's next generation
excerpt: A dusty pitch, one goalkeeper coach and dozens of teenagers who believe. The story behind Bugesera's talent pipeline.
author: Alice Mukamana
body: The pitch at Nyamata is not much to look at: compacted earth, two sets of rusty goalposts and a white line that gets repainted every Saturday morning. Yet it is where a growing number of Rwanda's young footballers are learning the game.

The academy is run by former Bugesera FC midfielder Emmanuel Rukundo, who returned to his hometown after a decade playing across the region. Sessions focus on technical repetition and small-sided games rather than results.
"We don't have a grass pitch, so we learn to control the ball on anything," Rukundo says. "By the time these boys go to a proper stadium, it feels easy."

Three academy graduates have already signed professional deals, and Bugesera FC now sends coaches to the sessions every week. Plans for a full-size artificial pitch are with the district, but funding is still short.

title: Ulimwengu: 'The derby is why you play football'
excerpt: Rayon's Burundian forward on the Kigali rivalry, the noise at Amahoro and the responsibility of wearing the number nine.
author: Diane Uwase
body: Jules Ulimwengu does not play down the occasion. For the Rayon Sports forward, the Kigali derby is the fixture that defines a season.
"I have played in different countries, but this atmosphere is special," Ulimwengu said. "The whole city stops. You cannot hear the coach from the sideline. That is why you play football."
The Burundian arrived at Rayon with a reputation for scoring in big games and has delivered five assists this season, many of them for Innocent Nshuti.
Rayon head into the afternoon level on points with APR at the top of the table, and Ulimwengu knows a win would change the mood around their run-in.
